function: Excluded (above_phy): DSAC reinforcement learning chooses UAV-user and UAV-satellite pairing, UAV trajectory, inter-satellite links and bit or semantic mode (p. 3, p. 8); no power, bandwidth or beam control.
notes: Reason above_phy. The PDF is the arXiv v3 preprint 'Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Resource Allocation for Hybrid Bit and Generative Semantic Communications in Space-Air-Ground Integrated Networks' (p. 1); it prints no DOI, so identity rests on title and topic. The only learned decision-maker is a distributed soft actor-critic agent. p. 3: 'The optimization variables include UAV-ground user pairing, UAV-satellite pairing, ISL selection, UAV dynamic planning, and semantic transmission mode selection.' p. 8 defines the action as a(t) = {R(t), O(t), L(t), Y(t), eps(t)}: pairings, UAV positions, inter-satellite link use and transmission mode. These are user association, relay choice and UAV trajectory, which the protocol lists as above the physical layer. Transmit powers and bandwidth are fixed, p. 9: 'the transmit powers of LEOs and UAVs are 1 W and 0.2 W' and 'the bandwidth for all transmissions is 10 MHz'; no beam, power or radio-resource control is learned, so the carve-out for learned control in satellite and aerial links does not apply. The semantic codec is source coding for images: p. 6 'VAE, BLIP-2, and CLIP use the most advanced pre-trained models and do not participate in model training', with VQE and UNet trained to compress and regenerate images; it does not perform detection, channel estimation, or beamforming. If the reviewer reads the bit or semantic mode choice as a physical-layer decision, the work would still be excluded under function (link adaptation and joint source-channel coding alone), so the decision exclude does not change. If the reviewer instead reads pairing, trajectory and mode choice as resource control for aerial links (area 6), note that the only external benchmark is the learned MAPPO algorithm (p. 9) and the other compared schemes are variants of the proposed one (p. 11), so no non-learned baseline for the controller appears. Simulation results exist (p. 9 to p. 11), so the results check is not the cause.
